turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... it's about my husband's sister. She’s been working this whole family business thing just so she can get control of the money. She's trying to push me completely out of making any decisions. And, well, no matter how folks try to smooth it over or tell me otherwise, I know what I’ve been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now, plain as day.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that her sister-in-law is plotting to take control of the family money and push her out, maintaining this belief despite others telling her otherwise.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt like you were hearing things that others around you couldn't hear, or that you were receiving special messages meant only for you?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or anything, and I'm not getting secret messages. I just see what she's doing right in front of me. turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you feel this same level of suspicion and mistrust toward other people in your life, such as friends, coworkers, or even other family members?
turns.patient_response:
No, not at all. I get along fine with my friends, and... well, the rest of the family is okay. I don't go around thinking everybody is out to get me or anything like that. 

It's really just her. I only don't trust her because of what she's actually doing with the money. With everyone else, I'm just my normal self. I trust people just fine when they aren't trying to steal from us.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reiterates their fixed belief that their sister-in-law is stealing money from them, demonstrating a persecutory delusion.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me about the specific evidence or actions you've seen that make you certain she is trying to steal the money?
turns.patient_response:
Well... I don't have, like, paperwork or bank statements to show you, if that's what you mean. I haven't gone digging through the books or anything like that. 

It's just... I can just tell by the way she acts around me when the money or the business comes up. You just know when someone is working against you. I don't really have a specific list of things to give you, or hard proof I can hand over. I just know what I'm seeing.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unshakeable belief that someone is working against them and trying to steal money, despite explicitly admitting they have no concrete evidence or proof to support this claim.

turns.doctor_question: How has this situation with your sister-in-law affected your ability to go about your daily routine or maintain your usual responsibilities?
turns.patient_response:
It hasn't really stopped me from doing what I need to do. I still keep up with my quilting group and choir practice, and I'm still going to my GED lessons and doing my senior walks just like I always have. 

It hasn't ruined my whole life or anything. Mostly, it's just changed how much I trust my husband's sister. I just have to be careful about which family gatherings I feel comfortable going to now, because I don't want to be around her if I can help it. But other than that, my day-to-day routine is pretty much the same.
